summary: This note covers the 1979 song "The Devil Went Down to Georgia" by Charlie Daniels, released as a single on Epic Records from the album Million Mile Reflections, with Rainbow Ride as the B-side. It lists the song's genres, length, songwriters, producer, and its place in Charlie Daniels's singles chronology alongside "Trudy" and "Mississippi." The song is described as written and performed by the Charlie Daniels Band.
one_line: A 1979 bluegrass and country rock single by Charlie Daniels from the album Million Mile Reflections.
key_facts: "The Devil Went Down to Georgia" is a single by Charlie Daniels from the album Million Mile Reflections.
The song's genres are listed as bluegrass, country, and country rock.
The label for the single was Epic.
The songwriters credited are Charlie Daniels, Tom Crain, "Taz" DiGregorio, Fred Edwards, Charles Hayward, and James W. Marshall.
The producers credited are John Boylan and Charlie Daniels.
In Charlie Daniels's singles chronology, "Trudy" was released in 1978 and "Mississippi" in 1979.
The song is described as written and performed by the Charlie Daniels Band.
The song was released on the Charlie Daniels Band's 1979 album Million Mile Reflections.
